solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expecting furious nurses to be irritated about hospital

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word for furious holds the rest inside it

parts.note: furious means wild with anger

indicators.note: the irritation word goes about, or around, the hospital letter

parts.note: to itch is to be irritated

explanation.surface: A furious patient, irritated with the hospital, is being looked after by nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like hospital staff, but it is the containment signal: 'about' and 'nurses' each wrap one piece around the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting a baby and being pregnant are the same state, an old-fashioned idiom.

clue.text: Out to lunch, ace ladies put out cold sandwiches

indicators.note: the ladies' loo letters sandwich the ace letter between them

parts.note: WC, water closet, stands for a lavatory such as the ladies
A is the card abbreviation for ace
KO, a knockout, puts a boxer out cold

explanation.surface: At lunchtime women wipe out the cold sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' is the British name for a women's toilet, hence WC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out to lunch is crazy, which is what wacko means in slang.

clue.text: Those out of the country have to visit relations

indicators.note: to visit is to go in, so the possession word goes into the relations word

parts.note: ties are links or relations
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Emigrants must go and see their families.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the country' looks like abroad, but it means not in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Townies are people who live in towns, not in rural areas.

clue.text: Game in boarding school subject to delay

indicators.note: boarding is getting on, so the word in gets on, into, the rest

parts.note: chem is short for chemistry
to defer is to delay

explanation.surface: A game at boarding school has to be put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarding school' looks like one phrase, but 'boarding' acts on 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a casino card game, a form of baccarat.

clue.text: Trendy? Don't fancy anything this colour!

parts.note: what is trendy is in
dig means fancy and O is nothing, so to dig nothing is not to fancy anything

explanation.surface: A fashion snob who finds nothing appealing in a particular shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet dye and shade, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Scrapping ad spoils broadcast

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An advert that ruins a programme should be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing something away is getting rid of it, a synonym of scrapping.

clue.text: Tailless mountain goat found in dry region

indicators.note: the trimmed goat is found inside the letters for dry

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. dry, not drinking

indicators.note: the goat word loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: the ibex is a wild mountain goat of the Alps

explanation.surface: A goat that has lost its tail turns up in an arid part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal here, not arid, so it supplies the outer letters rather than describing the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a Himalayan plateau now ruled by China as an autonomous region.

clue.text: Heads of two hundred orchids, all the same

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The tops of two hundred orchids all look alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the same' reads as identical flowers, but it means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Tho is an informal spelling of though, which means nevertheless.

clue.text: Irish and Polish turning to Mexican food

indicators.note: turning means the two pieces read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: Irish and Polish people switching to Mexican cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IRRUB to make BURRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish, a tortilla wrapped round a filling.

clue.text: Volatile person can put up radical fight

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a red is a left-wing radical
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: A hothead can stand up for a cause and pick a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinderbox is literally something that catches fire easily, so figuratively an explosive character.

clue.text: Beef tender and firm at point which cut by daughter

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: cut means the last letter of the word is chopped off

parts.note: where means at which point
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A recipe-like phrase about tender beef and some firm meat, cut by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims WHERE to WHER. 'Beef tender' looks like soft meat, but it is someone who tends beef cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowherd is a person who looks after cattle, and beef are cattle raised for meat.

clue.text: Dope men smuggled in pouch

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is British slang for information or gen, as in what's the SP?
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran means smuggled

explanation.surface: Men have sneaked drugs across a border in a little bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here it means inside information, SP. A sporran is the leather pouch worn at the front of a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The sporran is a purse or bag hung in front of a kilt, a kind of small pouch.

clue.text: Charm displayed by top Brit, every second

indicators.note: every second letter of the two words is taken, starting at the second

explanation.surface: A leading Briton shows off charm every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: Obi, also obeah, is a West African and Caribbean word for a fetish or charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is a fetish or amulet used in sorcery, a magical charm.

clue.text: Speaking well of video, cooing dreadfully

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Praising a video in which someone coos terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking well of' looks like praise, but the definition is 'Speaking well' and 'of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good voice means singing or talking clearly and strongly, an idiom for vocal fitness.

clue.text: Old language, very alluring at dances

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue, very seductive at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges ALLURING AT into ULGARLATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar Latin was the spoken Latin of the Roman Empire, ancestor of the Romance languages.

clue.text: Neighbours to come about eleven?

parts.note: to come about is to happen, to be
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football, is a side

explanation.surface: People next door are to come round at about eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'to': 'neighbours to' means next to. 'eleven' reads as a time but is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Being next to something is to be its neighbour, alongside it.

clue.text: Bags of waste English girl's put outside

parts.note: to blue money is British slang for squandering it

indicators.note: the girl's name is put outside the English letter, around it

parts.note: Jan is a girl's name, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A girl from England has put rubbish sacks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like sacks for waste, but it is British slang for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is old slang for loose trousers, and jeans are trousers.

clue.text: After arrest, fail to find weapon

indicators.note: the fail word comes after the arrest word

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch or arrest them
to bomb is to fail badly

explanation.surface: After an arrest, police fail to find a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail bomb is an explosive device packed with nails, a terrorist's weapon.

clue.text: Bishop presumably remaining longest on board launch

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the piece that stays longest on a board is the final one taken off it

explanation.surface: A chess bishop that survives the longest is set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship being launched, but it is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off of a rocket is its launch.

clue.text: Unify with European left? Somehow, that's not typical of the Dutch!

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A remark on European unification that the Netherlands is said to dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife (from 'my old Dutch', duchess), not people from the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour not typical of a spouse in the married-woman role, by the slang sense, is unbecoming in a wife.

clue.text: What we can hear: cheers welcoming one in Kansas City!

indicators.note: the sound piece and the thanks word welcome the one letter in between them
what we can hear gives the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: which means what, as in which one
ta and cheers both mean thank you in British English
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: We hear people cheering a newcomer in Kansas City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kansas City' looks like the name of the Missouri city, but it is a definition: a city in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in the state of Kansas.

clue.text: Cockney's to listen to the hits broadcast: what's to stop him?

indicators.note: broadcast means heard, as over the radio, so the sound gives the spelling

parts.words: Cockney's to listen to the hits
parts.note: a Cockney drops the h, so hear whacks comes out as 'ear 'wacks

explanation.surface: A Londoner wants to hear the chart hits on the radio, but something gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the dialect of East London, which drops initial H. 'hits' looks like pop songs but means whacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax building up in the ear canal blocks sound, so it stops the listener.

clue.text: Directory of people with houses around Cornwall?

indicators.note: the houses go around the Cornwall letters

parts.note: HO is short for house, twice for two houses
Cornwall is in the far south-west of England, so SW stands for it

explanation.surface: A list of residents with homes in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' marks Cornwall as an example of the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is a reference book listing notable people.

clue.text: In September in Washington it must … happen

parts.note: the ellipsis asks us to fill in after it must, giving be
Americans call autumn the fall

explanation.surface: In a Washington September something is bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: in September in Washington it must be fall, the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: To befall is to happen, often to someone, as misfortune does.

clue.text: Card game's to promote alternative to setter?

parts.note: the jack is a court card
RU is rugby union, a game, plus the 's
to sell a product is to promote it

explanation.surface: A bridge player says a card game is to be pushed rather than the setter's puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword's compiler, but it is a breed of gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dog breeds, so this terrier could stand in for a setter.

clue.text: Passes some task on after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of the two words are used

explanation.surface: Someone hands over part of a job before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks SKO from the middle of 'task on', and 'retiring' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something is to approve it, to give it the nod.

clue.text: Woolly gesture of indifference

definitions.meaning: a woolly is a knitted garment, here a short cardigan covering the shoulders
raising the shoulders to show one does not care

explanation.definitionFit: A shrug is both a cropped knitted cardigan and the lift of the shoulders that means so what.

clue.text: A note to send off that may get one's blessing?

parts.note: ti, also te, is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to shoo is to drive or send away

explanation.surface: A letter to be posted that might win someone's approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a letter, but it is a musical note; 'blessing' is the 'bless you' said after a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: People say bless you after a sneeze, so the sound of one earns a blessing.

clue.text: Conclusion to match, indeed, that's cut and dried

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: ay, or aye, means yes indeed

explanation.surface: The end of the match is, indeed, a foregone conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut and dried' looks like the idiom for settled, but grass is literally cut and dried.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass mown and left to dry becomes animal fodder.

clue.text: I want a rook to fly like a dove

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Someone wants a rook to fly as gracefully as a dove does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dove' looks like the bird, sitting nicely with rook; it means a peace-lover.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove opposes war, as against a hawk.

clue.text: Like flattery for example to interleave with work

indicators.note: interleaving shuffles one pair of letters in between the others, like riffling cards

parts.note: say means for example
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Flattery serves as an example that ought to be slipped into one's work.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a riffle, like shuffling two halves of a deck: the letters of the two pieces alternate, rather than one going whole inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapy talk is smooth and ingratiating, as flattery is; soft soap means flattery.

clue.text: Following a breather, performing grand exercise regime

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lung is the organ one breathes with
a performer is on, on stage
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: After a rest, someone does a big workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a pause, but it is a lung.
explanation.definitionFit: Falun Gong is a Chinese spiritual practice built around qigong exercises and meditation.
